independence_caveat: Superseded on 2026-08-24. The batch was first checked in the producing context, which found and corrected two claims but - as that record itself warned - could not catch an error of understanding shared by the authoring and checking passes. A genuinely independent clean-context review was then run and found FIVE further defects the same-context pass had missed, two of them authored by this session and three predating it. That is the exposure OPEN-G1-002 described, realised. All are fixed.
scope: The 8 cards of batch G1: 4 new cards and 4 enrichment limbs, drawn from submissions S003 and S004.
method: Every figure and date was checked against an official or primary source, not against another MIW card.
Every regulation citation was checked for the right instrument AND the right applicability limb.
Each new card was checked against the negative search that authorised it, to confirm it answers the ask the candidate actually reported rather than a nearby one.
Each enrichment was checked to confirm it adds the missing limb and does not restate what the card already said.

corrections_made_during_review.what: The shipbuilding package was first drafted from a secondary source giving a July 2026 date and an SBFAP 2.0 figure of Rs 18,090 crore.
corrections_made_during_review.resolution: Both were wrong. The Union Cabinet approved the Rs 69,725 crore package on 24 September 2025, and the SBFAS corpus is Rs 24,736 crore to 31 March 2036. Confirmed by the arithmetic: 24,736 + 19,989 + 25,000 = 69,725 exactly. The card carries the corrected figures.

corrections_made_during_review.what: A draft of the newbuilding card treated the IMO Net-Zero Framework as an applicable requirement.
corrections_made_during_review.resolution: It is approved at MEPC 83 (April 2025) but NOT adopted - the October 2025 extraordinary session was adjourned for twelve months. The card now states the status explicitly and flags claiming it as in force as a currency failure.

authority_checked: LSA Code 4.4 - lifeboat not less than 7.3 m, maximum 150 persons, at least 6 knots loaded, at least 2 knots towing a 25-person liferaft, fuel for 24 h at 6 knots. All five confirmed.
LSA Code 5.1 - rescue boat 3.8 m to 8.5 m, at least five seated persons plus one on a stretcher, 6 knots maintained for at least 4 hours. All three confirmed.
SOLAS III/17 - rescue boat recovery in not more than 5 minutes in moderate sea conditions; launch and recovery with the ship making up to 5 knots.
SOLAS III/31 is the cargo ship carriage regulation and III/21 the passenger ship one. The card says so and warns against quoting III/21 for a cargo ship.
watch_items: Two distinct 5-minute figures exist in SOLAS III - readiness for launching, and recovery. This card claims only the RECOVERY figure, which is the one that distinguishes a rescue boat from a lifeboat, and it agrees with the live QB2_E#q1.
cards.distinctness: QB2_E#q1's deep-dive already answers the narrow dual-role sub-point ('can a lifeboat also act as a rescue boat?'). That is one line inside another card's deep-dive, not the examinable ask. Nothing in the bank contrasts the two craft on purpose, dimensions, capacity, endurance or recovery duty. The overlap is acknowledged in the card, which treats dual role as a section rather than as the whole answer.
cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the independent finding was fixed; see independent_review.

authority_checked: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 18 - bunker delivery note retained 3 years, representative sample 12 months.
The standard time charter forms named (NYPE, BALTIME, SHELLTIME) are correct for a time charter, not a voyage charter.
Off-hire is stated as a clause-dependent test rather than an automatic consequence, which is correct and is the trap in the question.
watch_items: The card deliberately keeps the BDN in the answer while flagging it as statutory in origin, because the examiner's exclusion was of statutory CERTIFICATES and the BDN is commercial evidence. This is a judgement call and is stated openly in the card.
cards.distinctness: QB1_B#q17, QB9_B#q3 and QB9_B#q4 were read in full. None enumerates the document set a time charter runs on.

authority_checked: Union Cabinet approval of the Rs 69,725 crore package on 24 September 2025.
SBFAS extended to 31 March 2036, corpus Rs 24,736 crore including about Rs 4,001 crore of shipbreaking credit note.
Shipbuilding Development Scheme Rs 19,989 crore, targeting 4.5 million GT of annual capacity.
Maritime Development Fund Rs 25,000 crore = Maritime Investment Fund Rs 20,000 crore (49% Government of India) + Interest Incentivisation Fund Rs 5,000 crore, announced Union Budget 2025-26.
Internal consistency check: the three limbs sum exactly to the headline figure.
watch_items: This is the most currency-sensitive card in the batch. The figures are dated in the card itself so a future reader can see what they were current to.
A secondary source quoting 'SBFAP 2.0, Rs 18,090 crore' was rejected as inconsistent with the official component figures.
cards.distinctness: QB9_D#q5 (GIFT City) and QB10_A#q3 (Sagarmala) were read and rejected: a financial-centre card and a port-infrastructure card respectively. The card names the Sagarmala confusion as the trap.

authority_checked: IACS UR E26 and E27 - mandatory for ships contracted for construction on or after 1 July 2024. Confirmed.

IMO Net-Zero Framework - approved MEPC 83 April 2025, NOT adopted; the October 2025 extraordinary session was adjourned for twelve months and reconvenes late 2026. Stated as status, not as requirement.
Hong Kong Convention in force 26 June 2025.
SOLAS II-1/3-10 Goal-Based Standards apply to bulk carriers and oil tankers.
Code on Noise Levels On Board Ships, Res. MSC.337(91).
watch_items: The reconvened extraordinary session date is given as 'late 2026' rather than a specific day, because sources differ between November and December 2026 and the examinable point is the STATUS, not the date. If a precise date is later confirmed it can be added by correction.
cards.distinctness: Negative search over all 721 live questions returned zero hits on ship design, newbuilding, yard, specification and building contract.
cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the independent finding was fixed; see independent_review.

authority_checked: GIC Re is the sole designated Indian reinsurer for the obligatory cession - there is no order of preference among several bodies for that cession.
IRDAI has fixed the obligatory cession at 4% for insurances attaching 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, with terrorism premium and premium ceded to the nuclear pool at NIL.
watch_items: The percentage is set annually, so this limb carries a financial-year stamp and will need rechecking for FY 2027-28.
cards.distinctness: The card already answered the parent ask and the 'why'. Only the India limb was missing, and only the India limb was added.

authority_checked: Marine Spatial Planning in India is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences through the National Centre for Coastal Research, under the Indo-Norway Integrated Ocean Initiative (MoU 2019).
Puducherry launched India's first MSP framework; Puducherry and Lakshadweep were the two pilot sites.
Odisha rolled out its Marine Spatial Plan on 16 April 2026, the first full State as distinct from a Union Territory pilot.
watch_items: The Odisha item is four months old at authoring and is the freshest fact in the batch. It is the strongest single answer to the examiner's actual ask for an established Indian example.
cards.distinctness: The card already carried the definition, process and an India-facing regulatory box, but named no established Indian MSP site. Corroboration: this card's CE Oral Tip was already headed 'Kochi MMD Focus (Examiner Rajappan)', and Rajappan is the external examiner on the August panel - a fresh sitting confirming an attribution the bank had already recorded.
cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the independent finding was fixed; see independent_review.

authority_checked: IMO Res. A.1192(33) already cited by the card, adopted 6 December 2023, urging action against dark/shadow fleet operations including verification of insurance and AIS integrity - which is the authority the added due-diligence limb rests on.

The checks listed are all genuinely available to a joining officer: registry and ownership history, IACS class status, International Group P&I entry, AIS continuity, OFAC/EU/UK sanctions screening, Equasis and the PSC detention record.
watch_items: The limb deliberately states that no single check is decisive and the pattern is. Presenting any one of them as a test would be wrong and would mislead a candidate.
cards.distinctness: The card fully answered 'what is the shadow fleet'. The tested limb - how a joining officer satisfies himself - was absent. This is preserved as an enrichment of the existing card rather than a new card, because flattening an examiner follow-up into an unrelated card is how the bank grows duplicates.
cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the independent finding was fixed; see independent_review.

authority_checked: Container freight indices: Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) and China Containerized Freight Index (CCFI), with Drewry's World Container Index and the Freightos Baltic Index as the other widely quoted series.
Dry bulk: the Baltic Exchange Baltic Dry Index, composed of the Capesize, Panamax, Supramax and Handysize sub-indices and assessed from a reporting broker panel.
Tankers: the Baltic Dirty and Clean Tanker Indices, with rates expressed on the Worldscale nominal scale as a percentage of the WS100 flat rate for the voyage.
No dated regulatory claim is made in this limb, so it carries no currency exposure - deliberately, because market structure is stable where rate levels are not.
watch_items: Index NAMES are stable; index LEVELS are not, so the limb quotes no rate figure. A card that quoted a BDI value would be stale within days.
cards.distinctness: QB8_A#q3 already explained how a rate is FORMED - supply and demand, BAF, THC, peak season surcharges - and named the SCFI in passing. The examiner asked where the number is obtained. /Baltic Exchange|BDI|SCFI|shipbroker|broker/ returned only QB9_H#q15, which defines the broker's role rather than the rate source.
cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the independent finding was fixed; see independent_review.

batch_level_findings: No G1 card names an examiner. This was checked mechanically as well as by reading, and the derived examiner index confirms a zero relationship delta at 958 across the batch.

The four new cards match their destination file's own card template, which differs between QB2_E, QB9_D and QB1_C in the practice-block form, the deep-dive markup and the footer. All 86 pages pass the question-text and DOM-nesting gate at 7527 controls.
QB3_G is a CRLF page and remained pure CRLF after the enrichment; no file acquired mixed line endings.

Submission S004 produced ZERO new cards. Seven of its eight occurrences resolved to existing cards or to administrative questions, and the eighth is held as ambiguous. That is the first August submission the bank absorbed almost entirely, and it is evidence the corpus is maturing rather than evidence the submission was thin.

S004 also exposed three parser defects that would each have LOST or LEAKED evidence: a space before the question separator ('1 .Written status.') dropped two occurrences into context silently; an attribution marker carrying its content inline ('Senthil : tqm, new acts and difference between act and rule.') was neither a marker nor a numbered question and vanished entirely; and a pasted chat transcript would have carried a named third party into a committed record. All three are fixed, and the first 32 occurrences were proven byte-identical afterwards.

independent_review.mechanism: A reviewer with no access to the producing reasoning. It was given only the card anchors and a rubric, and was explicitly barred from reading the adjudication record, the batch manifests, this review record and the commit history. It was instructed to verify against issuing-body text and never by finding a second site that repeats a claim.
independent_review.outcome: 5 of 8 items required a fix. All fixes applied; none left live.

findings.defect: The 5-knot headway figure was attached to RECOVERY. SOLAS III/17.1 puts it on LAUNCHING; recovery is governed by a time - not more than 5 minutes in moderate sea conditions, III/17.3. The error appeared five times in the card.
findings.fix: All five corrected, and the distinction is now stated explicitly as a trap.
findings.note: The same conflation was then found twice more in QB2_E#q1, which predates this session and which the reviewer was not asked to check. Both corrected.

findings.defect: Cited MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 21 and 22 as EEDI and SEEMP. That is the pre-2021 numbering. MEPC.328(76), in force 1 Nov 2022, renumbered Chapter 4: Reg. 22 attained EEDI, Reg. 24 required EEDI, Reg. 26 SEEMP, Reg. 28 operational carbon intensity. Reg. 21 is now Functional requirements. A candidate would have quoted a four-year-stale citation from the reference box.
findings.fix: Corrected, and the stale numbering is now flagged in the card as a common wrong answer. The GBS scope limb was also completed - SOLAS II-1/3-10 applies to oil tankers and bulk carriers of 150 m and above contracted on or after 1 July 2016 - and the Net-Zero extraordinary session date sharpened to 4 December 2026, subject to confirmation by MEPC 85.

findings.defect: Two defects. MINE: the card said Odisha 'rolled out its Marine Spatial Plan on 16 April 2026'. What happened that day was the SIGNING OF AN MoU between the Odisha S&T Department and NCCR to prepare and implement a plan - not the publication of a finished one. PRE-EXISTING: the reference box cited IMO Res. A.857(20) for VTS guidelines, which was REVOKED by A.1158(32) on 15 December 2021.
findings.fix: Both corrected; the MoU wording now warns the candidate to be precise if pressed.

findings.defect: The Casualty Link said the 2023 tanker Pablo casualty produced an oil slick. She was in BALLAST and no spill was reported. And the reference box labelled SOLAS V/19-1 as AIS; V/19-1 is long-range identification and tracking (LRIT).
findings.fix: The LRIT labelling corrected - and it is the stronger dark-fleet answer, because LRIT reports to the flag State and cannot be switched off from the bridge. The Pablo wording is carried to the correction record.

findings.defect: Described the Baltic Dry Index as built from Capesize, Panamax, Supramax AND Handysize. Baltic Exchange Circular 08/18 removed Handysize from the BDI on 1 March 2018; the index has been weighted 40% Capesize / 30% Panamax / 30% Supramax since. Handysize is reported separately as the BHSI. The card was describing the pre-2018 four-way split.
findings.fix: Corrected with the weightings and the date, which turns a liability into a discriminator.

independent_review.qb9d_q12_verification: Every Indian ship-finance figure was independently confirmed against the PIB release and the Cabinet announcement: package Rs 69,725 crore approved 24 September 2025; SBFAS Rs 24,736 crore to 31 March 2036 including about Rs 4,001 crore of shipbreaking credit note; SbDS Rs 19,989 crore targeting 4.5 million GT annually; MDF Rs 25,000 crore = MIF Rs 20,000 crore at 49% Government of India plus IIF Rs 5,000 crore. The three limbs sum exactly to the headline. The reviewer also checked FORWARD for revision and found none as at 24 Aug 2026.
independent_review.out_of_scope_finding: The reviewer could not avoid seeing that QB8_A#q3 ships raw draft artefacts to candidates OUTSIDE the section it was asked to review: literal '[cite: 1]' markers in the reference box, a <pre> block duplicating the reference box in plain ASCII, literal '---' separators, the word 'arrow' where a glyph belonged, and a stale correction footer reading QB8 Q16 inside a card whose own footer reads Q3. Registered as OPEN-G1-007; deliberately NOT mixed into this batch.
